walkthroughs.body_html:
Water & Aquatic Food Systems — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Water & Aquatic Food Systems brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Water & Aquatic Food Systems.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Schaefer's maximum sustainable yield model dates from:
Newfoundland cod fishery moratorium was imposed in:

options: Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Common land in medieval Britain.
Acid rain falling on the ocean.
Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH.

mcqs.q: How do greenhouse gases warm Earth?
options: They reflect sunlight back to Earth.
They block heat from escaping into space (like a literal lid).
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
They absorb infrared radiation emitted by Earth's surface and re-radiate some back down.

mcqs.q: What does the 'tragedy of the commons' describe?
options: Shared resources tend to be overexploited because individuals benefit personally while sharing costs.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
It is a play about poor people.
Common land in medieval Britain.
